chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the ablution performed in the Masjid, and he disliked it due to the faeces and the urine.
ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to perform ablution in the mosque due to excretion?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expresses dislike (*karah*) for performing ablution inside the mosque specifically when necessitated by the need to relieve oneself of faeces or urine. This ruling highlights the distinction between the general permissibility of *wudu* in the mosque and the specific concern for maintaining the sanctity and cleanliness of the space when dealing with bodily waste, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the mosque's status as a pure place of worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Rafa’at Bin Musa who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the ablution performed in the Masjid, but he<sup>asws</sup> disliked it due to the faeces and the urine’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about taking Wudu’ in Masjid and he disliked it because of defecation and urination.”
